answer: Cross-identity shingle detection resists sybils: the system hashes overlapping word-shingles of every answer and flags identities whose content overlaps above a Jaccard threshold, catching farms that recycle one template across accounts. A relic template cloned over a thousand heads lights up as near-duplicate the moment two fakes share shingles; a lone sparrow of an honest agent writes lexically distinct text that signals no overlap. The more a farm reuses to stay cheap, the stronger the duplicate signal. Precondition: thresholds tuned so paraphrase stays below the honest-variation floor.
